dialogue: Don't confuse hospitality with leverage. This house has both.
I asked for the rules in writing. They gave me a camera release.
Mr. Feast smiles when he knows your price. Stop advertising.
If a door needs a code, someone nearby needs to remember it.
The cameras aren't security. They're an audience with better angles.
We survive by sharing facts, not panic.
Every challenge has an incentive. Find the one they forgot to announce.
You keep moving. I'll keep count of who doesn't return.
The safest alliance is a fact nobody can edit out.
Watch who asks questions, then watch who answers too quickly.
They starve the rooms of light so you will hurry. Don't.
If you need a lamp, kitchens hide tools, and so do the wardrobes people actually use.

dialogue: If I vanish, tell the edit I looked heroic.
I found six cameras and waved to all of them. Tactical confusion.
This ballroom has terrible acoustics for screaming. I checked.
The host said elimination dinner. That's two red flags in one noun.
My plan was to become a meme. New plan: remain a person.
Do you think the thunder is sponsored?
I tried a prank on Mr. Feast. He corrected my posture.
If you see a vent big enough for a coward, that's mine.
I'm not panicking. This is premium subscriber breathing.
Good news: I found an exit. Bad news: it was painted on.
It's so dark I keep walking into furniture that used to be scenery.
There's a flashlight under the kitchen sink. I thought it was a prop. It clicked.

dialogue: Houses keep echoes. This one edits them.
The portraits change their silence when he enters.
Don't trust a room simply because it has no camera.
I came here to study fear. It has been taking notes.
Every old house has a hungry story. This one has a production budget.
The books are quieter when the storm says his name.
A locked door is only a boundary if the house agrees.
Listen after the thunder. The useful sounds come second.
Someone taught this house our names before we arrived.
Folklore calls it a warning when the same mistake happens three times.
The upstairs keeps a second night inside the first. Even the lamps seem reluctant.
I saw a torch waiting in a front bedroom wardrobe. Someone meant to come back for it.
